title: 8 Asian students counted at Jefferson Parkway Elementary for 2024-25
text:
Eight Asian students attended Jefferson Parkway Elementary School in the 2024-25 school year, matching the figure from the prior year, data from the Georgia Department of Education showed.
The school’s total enrollment reached 421 students in 2024-25. Asian students comprised 2% of the overall student population, which represented the smallest ethnic group at the school.
Jefferson Parkway Elementary operates in the Coweta County School District, which is headquartered in Newnan.
Of the 29 schools in Coweta County School District, East Coweta High School had the highest Asian student enrollment in 2024-25, reporting 116 students.
Statewide, Georgia public schools enrolled more than 1.7 million students , according to the Georgia Department of Education’s Fiscal Year 2026-1 report. The largest share attended elementary grades with 787,206 students (45.9%), followed by 388,733 in middle school (22.7%), and 539,092 in high school (31.4%).
After the pandemic, chronic absenteeism poses a persistent challenge in Georgia. In 2024, 20.7% of students missed at least 10% of all school days, the Georgia Department of Education reported. In response, the department rolled out a statewide campaign that includes a real-time attendance dashboard and outreach to districts with high needs in order to increase daily participation.
For 2025, a bill updating attendance laws passed the Georgia legislature, prohibiting expulsions for absenteeism alone . The statute requires new reporting protocols and supports alternative diploma pathways for students.
By 2026, Georgia’s average student-to-teacher ratio stood at about 14:1 , outperforming the national average of 15:1 .
